details: Bitcoin's price surged above $74,000 on May 29, rebounding from an intraday low, following reports of a tentative agreement between the U.S. and Iran to extend a ceasefire and reopen the Strait of Hormuz. This de-escalation of geopolitical tensions, confirmed by former President Donald Trump, led to increased optimism in financial markets, with global stocks rising and oil prices declining. The removal of the naval blockade in the strategic Strait of Hormuz is seen as a significant de-escalation, positively impacting market sentiment across various assets, including cryptocurrencies.
title: Bitcoin Surges to $74K Amid Hopes for US-Iran Ceasefire

details: U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent announced on May 29 that the United States has seized approximately $1 billion in Iranian cryptocurrency assets. This action is part of a broader campaign to disrupt Tehran's financial networks, with Bessent stating the funds were "stolen from the Iranian people" and used for sanctions evasion. The cumulative figure reflects ongoing efforts, including previous freezes of stablecoins like Tether (USDT) linked to Iran's Revolutionary Guard Corps.
title: US Treasury Seizes $1 Billion in Iranian Crypto Assets
